chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Harun ibn Muslim from Ali ibn Hassan from Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

My father was asked about visiting the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: Pray in the mosques around it, and it will suffice in all places that you say: Peace be upon the Guardians of Allah and His elites. Peace be upon the trustworthy ones of Allah and His beloved ones. Peace be upon the helpers of Allah and His caliphs. Peace be upon the places of recognition of Allah. Peace be upon the dwellings of the remembrance of Allah. Peace be upon those who manifest the command and prohibition of Allah. Peace be upon the callers to Allah. Peace be upon those settled in the pleasure of Allah. Peace be upon those refined in the obedience of Allah. Peace be upon the pointers to Allah. Peace be upon those who, whoever befriends them has befriended Allah, and whoever is inimical to them has been inimical to Allah, and whoever recognizes them has recognized Allah, and whoever is ignorant of them has been ignorant of Allah, and whoever holds fast to them has held fast to Allah, and whoever loosens from them has loosened from Allah.

I testify to Allah that I am at peace with those who are at peace with you, and at war with those who are at war with you, a believer in your secrets and your public declarations, entrusting all of that to you. May Allah curse the enemies of the Progeny of Muhammad from the Jinn and humans, and I disavow to Allah from them, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny.

This will suffice for all visits, and you should frequent sending blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny, and name them one by one by their names, and disavow to Allah from their enemies, and choose for yourself from supplication whatever you like, and for the believing men and women.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ: Sending blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and protocol for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Rida (as) establishes a flexible framework for Ziyarat, affirming that while visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (as) is meritorious, the essential spiritual connection is maintained through specific salutations and prayers in any mosque. It highlights the Shia doctrine of 'Wala' and 'Bara' (loyalty and enmity) by linking the recognition of the Imams directly to the knowledge and worship of Allah, a concept rooted in the principle of 'Tawassul' through the Ahl al-Bayt. The text serves as a comprehensive model for all Ziyarat visits, emphasizing personal supplication alongside the prescribed declarations of peace with friends and war with enemies of the Imams.
